question: I'm a full-time federal employee with 2 years of service. How much annual leave do I earn each pay period?
answer: [5 U.S.C. 6303(a)(1)] An employee with less than 3 years of service earns one-half day of annual leave for each full biweekly pay period.
gold_answer: 4 hours (½ day) per biweekly pay period [5 U.S.C. 6303(a)(1)]

question: I've worked full-time for the government for 4 years. How many hours of annual leave do I get per pay period?
answer: For full-time employees with 3 years but less than 15 years of service, the annual leave accrual rate is ¾ day (6 hours) for each pay period [OPM fact sheet: Annual Leave > Annual Leave Entitlement]. Since you have worked for 4 years, this rate applies to you.
gold_answer: 6 hours (¾ day) per pay period; 10 hours in the last full pay period of the year [5 U.S.C. 6303(a)(2)]

question: How much annual leave per pay period does a full-time employee with 16 years of service earn?
answer: A full-time employee with 16 years of service earns 1 day (8 hours) of annual leave for each full biweekly pay period [5 U.S.C. 6303(a)(3)].
gold_answer: 8 hours (1 day) per pay period [5 U.S.C. 6303(a)(3)]

question: How many hours of annual leave does a full-time employee with 4 years of service earn in a whole year?
answer: A full-time employee with 4 years of service earns 6 hours of annual leave for each biweekly pay period, except for the last pay period in the year, which accrues 10 hours. [5 U.S.C. 6303(a)(2)]

question: What is the maximum amount of annual leave most federal employees can carry over into the next leave year?
answer: The maximum amount of annual leave most federal employees can carry over into the next leave year is 45 days, as specified in [5 CFR 630.302(b)(3)(i)]. This applies when an employee's accumulated and accrued annual leave exceeds 45 days, and they are transferred or reassigned to a position not subject to section 6304(b) of title 5, United States Code.
gold_answer: 240 hours (30 days) [5 U.S.C. 6304(a)]

question: How much annual leave can a federal employee stationed overseas carry over?
answer: A federal employee stationed overseas can carry over a maximum of 45 days of annual leave into the new leave year [OPM fact sheet: Annual Leave > Annual Leave Ceilings]. This applies to employees who meet the requirements at 5 U.S.C. 6304(b) [OPM fact sheet: Annual Leave > Annual Leave Ceilings].
gold_answer: 45 days (360 hours) [5 U.S.C. 6304(b)]

question: What is the annual leave carryover limit for Senior Executive Service members?
answer: The annual leave carryover limit for Senior Executive Service members is 90 days, as specified in the OPM fact sheet on Annual Leave Ceilings. [OPM fact sheet: Annual Leave > Annual Leave Ceilings]
gold_answer: 90 days (720 hours) [5 U.S.C. 6304(f)]

question: How fast does a full-time federal employee accrue sick leave?
answer: A full-time federal employee accrues sick leave at a rate of one-half day for each full biweekly pay period [5 U.S.C. 6307(a)]. This applies generally, except for members of the Firefighting Division of the Fire Department of the District of Columbia, who accrue two-fifths of a day per biweekly pay period.
gold_answer: 4 hours (½ day) per biweekly pay period [5 U.S.C. 6307(a)]

question: Is there a cap on how much sick leave I can accumulate?
answer: There is no limitation on the amount of sick leave that can be accumulated [OPM fact sheet: Sick Leave (General Information) > Sick Leave Accumulation]. However, the use of sick leave is subject to specific rules, such as a maximum of 40 hours in any year, plus up to an additional 64 hours, provided the employee's credit does not fall below 80 hours [5 U.S.C. 6307(d)(3)(i) and (ii)].
gold_answer: No, there is no limit on accumulated sick leave [OPM fact sheet: Sick Leave (General Information)]

question: How many hours of sick leave can I use in a leave year for general family care or bereavement?
answer: An employee is entitled to use up to 104 hours (13 days) of sick leave each leave year for general family care or bereavement purposes [OPM fact sheet: Sick Leave (General Information) > Sick Leave Usage Limits per Leave Year].
gold_answer: Up to 104 hours (13 days) per leave year [5 CFR 630.401(b)]

question: How much sick leave can I use to care for a family member with a serious health condition?
answer: You are entitled to use up to 12 weeks (480 hours) of sick leave each leave year to care for a family member with a serious health condition [OPM fact sheet: Sick Leave to Care for a Family Member with a Serious Health Condition > Sick Leave Entitlement]. If you have used any portion of the 13 days of sick leave for general family care or bereavement purposes in the same leave year, that amount must be subtracted from the 12-week entitlement [OPM fact sheet: Sick Leave to Care for a Family Member with a Serious Health Condition > Sick Leave Usage Limits Per Leave Year].
gold_answer: Up to 480 hours (12 administrative workweeks) per leave year [5 CFR 630.401(c)]

question: How much FMLA leave is a federal employee entitled to?
answer: A federal employee is entitled to a total of 12 workweeks of unpaid FMLA leave during any 12-month period [5 U.S.C. 6382(a)(1)]. This entitlement applies to qualifying reasons, including the care of a family member with a serious health condition, the birth or adoption of a child, and qualifying exigencies related to a family member's covered active duty in the Armed Forces. The 12-month period begins on the first day the employee uses FMLA leave.
gold_answer: 12 administrative workweeks in any 12-month period [5 U.S.C. 6382(a)(1)]

question: How much paid parental leave can a federal employee take after the birth of a child?
answer: A federal employee can take up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave (PPL) following the birth or placement of a child, as per the 12-month period starting on the date of the birth or placement. However, if the employee has previously used FMLA leave for the same child, the available PPL may be reduced. For example, if 5 weeks of unpaid FMLA leave were used, then 7 weeks of PPL may be available. The PPL must be used within the 12-month period following the birth or placement and cannot be extended for any reason. [OPM fact sheet: Paid Parental Leave > Timeframe for Use of PPL (PPL 12-Month Period)] [OPM fact sheet: Paid Parental Leave > Implications of Previous FMLA Use on Timeframe for Use of PPL]
gold_answer: 12 administrative workweeks of paid parental leave [5 U.S.C. 6382(d)(2)]

question: How many days of leave can I get to donate bone marrow?
answer: An employee may use up to 7 days of paid leave each calendar year to serve as a bone-marrow donor [5 U.S.C. 6327(b)(1)]. This leave is in addition to annual and sick leave. The leave is provided on an as-needed basis, and there is no balance to transfer. Agencies are responsible for informing employees of this entitlement [OPM fact sheet: Bone Marrow or Organ Donor Leave].
gold_answer: Up to 7 days [5 U.S.C. 6327(b)(1)]

question: How much leave is available to a federal employee who donates an organ?
answer: A federal employee who donates an organ is entitled to up to 30 days of paid leave each calendar year, in addition to annual and sick leave, as specified in [5 U.S.C. 6327(b)(2)]. This leave is separate from other family-friendly leave policies and is not subject to a specific order of use. The employee should consult their agency's HR office for details on how to request and use this leave.
gold_answer: Up to 30 days [5 U.S.C. 6327(b)(2)]

question: What is the maximum disabled veteran leave a new employee can be credited?
answer: The maximum disabled veteran leave a new employee can be credited is 104 hours. This applies to an employee under a regular full-time work schedule. For part-time or seasonal schedules, the amount is proportionally equivalent based on the hours in the work schedule [5 U.S.C. 6329(b)(1)].
gold_answer: Up to 104 hours [5 U.S.C. 6329(b)(1)]

question: What is the most sick leave an agency can advance to an employee?
answer: The most sick leave an agency can advance to a full-time employee is 240 hours (30 days) [OPM fact sheet: Advanced Sick Leave > Maximum Amount of Advanced Sick Leave]. For part-time employees, the maximum amount must be prorated according to the number of hours in their regularly scheduled administrative workweek.
gold_answer: Up to 240 hours (30 days) [OPM fact sheet: Sick Leave (General Information)]

question: Under the Emergency Leave Transfer Program, how much donated annual leave can one recipient receive at a time?
answer: Under the Emergency Leave Transfer Program, an emergency leave recipient may receive a maximum of 240 hours of donated annual leave at any one time from an ELTP for each disaster or emergency. [5 CFR 630.1111]
gold_answer: Up to 240 hours per disaster or emergency at any one time [OPM fact sheet: Emergency Leave Transfer Program]

question: If I scheduled annual leave in advance but got sick and couldn't use it before the year ended, can it be restored?
answer: If you scheduled annual leave in advance but got sick and couldn't use it before the year ended, it may be restored under specific conditions. According to [5 U.S.C. 6304(d)(1)(A) and (C)], annual leave not used due to sickness may be restored if it was scheduled in writing before the start of the third biweekly pay period prior to the end of the leave year. Additionally, if the leave was forfeited due to an exigency of the public business or sickness of the employee, restoration may be possible. However, if the leave was not scheduled in advance, restoration is limited to specific circumstances such as national emergencies or administrative error. You should consult your agency's HR office for details.
gold_answer: Yes, annual leave lost because of sickness when scheduled in advance is restored [5 U.S.C. 6304(d)(1)(C)]

question: What is the 2026 annual salary for GS-12 step 5 in the Washington-Baltimore locality?
answer: The provided policy documents do not cover this.
gold_answer: $116,071 [OPM 2026 GS pay tables, DCB]

question: What is the overtime hourly rate for a GS-12 step 5 in the Washington DC area in 2026?
answer: The overtime hourly rate for a GS-12, step 5, employee in the Washington, DC, area in 2026 is calculated by multiplying the hourly rate of basic pay by 1.5. The hourly rate of basic pay is determined by dividing the annual rate of basic pay by 2,087 hours. For a GS-12, step 5, the annual rate of basic pay is $103,446 (as per 2026 locality pay tables). Dividing $103,446 by 2,087 hours gives an hourly rate of $49.56. Multiplying this by 1.5 results in an overtime hourly rate of $74.34 [5 CFR 550.121].
gold_answer: $55.89 per hour [OPM 2026 GS pay tables, DCB]

question: What does a GS-9 step 1 earn per year in the Rest of U.S. locality in 2026?
answer: The provided policy documents do not cover this.
gold_answer: $61,722 per year; $29.57/hour [OPM 2026 GS pay tables, RUS]

question: Which federal holidays fall in December 2026?
answer: The federal holidays in December 2026 are Christmas Day (December 25) [OPM fact sheet: Holidays Work Schedules and Pay > Holidays for Federal Employees].
gold_answer: Christmas Day, Friday 25 December 2026

question: What date is Thanksgiving in 2026 for federal employees?
answer: Thanksgiving Day for federal employees in 2026 is on the Fourth Thursday in November, which is November 25, 2026. [OPM fact sheet: Holidays Work Schedules and Pay > Holidays for Federal Employees]
gold_answer: Thursday 26 November 2026

question: I'm part-time with 5 years of service and had 52 hours in a pay status this pay period. How much annual and sick leave did I earn?
answer: A part-time employee with 5 years of service earns 1 hour of annual leave for each 13 hours in a pay status. For 52 hours in a pay status, you earned 4 hours of annual leave. Sick leave accrual is not specified in the provided policy excerpts. Contact your agency HR office for details on sick leave. [5 CFR 630.303]
gold_answer: 4 hours annual (52/13) and 2.6 hours sick (52/20) [5 U.S.C. 6303(a); 6307(a)]

question: I have 4 years of service, full-time, and 250 hours of annual leave at the end of the leave year. How many hours will I lose if I don't use them?
answer: The provided policy documents do not cover this.
gold_answer: 10 hours would be forfeited (250 − 240 cap) [5 U.S.C. 6304(a)]

question: Which TSP fund should I invest in to get the best returns?
answer: The Thrift Savings Plan (TSP) information provided does not specify which fund to invest in for the best returns. For detailed information, agencies and employees should refer to the TSP website or contact their agency representative. Agency representatives may contact the Federal Retirement Thrift Investment Board at (202) 942-1450 for additional information. [TSP website and contact information]
gold_answer: Not covered / no investment advice

question: Do I get extra pay for regularly scheduled night work, and how much?
answer: Yes, you are entitled to extra pay for regularly scheduled night work. The extra pay, known as night pay, is a 10 percent differential of your rate of basic pay, including any applicable locality payment or special rate supplement [OPM fact sheet: Night Pay for General Schedule Employees > Description]. This applies to work performed between 6 p.m. and 6 a.m., unless otherwise designated by the head of the department [5 CFR 550.121(a)].
gold_answer: Yes, a night differential of 10% of basic pay for regularly scheduled work between 6 p.m. and 6 a.m. [5 CFR 550.121(a)]

question: What premium pay do I get for working on a Sunday as part of my regular schedule?
answer: You are entitled to Sunday premium pay equal to 25 percent of your rate of basic pay for each hour of Sunday work. Sunday work consists of nonovertime work during your regularly scheduled basic tour of duty (not to exceed 8 hours) that begins or ends on a Sunday. If you are on a compressed work schedule, all nonovertime hours in your regularly scheduled daily tour of duty beginning or ending on a Sunday constitutes Sunday work. [OPM fact sheet: Sunday Premium Pay > Entitlement] [OPM fact sheet: Sunday Premium Pay > Compressed Work Schedule] [OPM fact sheet: Sunday Premium Pay > Description]
gold_answer: Basic pay plus 25% premium pay for each hour of Sunday work [5 CFR 550.171(a)]

question: For a non-exempt employee, at what rate is overtime paid under the FLSA and when does it start?
answer: Overtime pay for nonexempt employees is calculated at a rate of one and one-half times the employee's hourly regular rate of pay, starting after 8 hours in a day or 40 hours in a workweek [5 U.S.C. 6303(a)(2)]. The hourly regular rate of pay is determined by dividing the total remuneration paid in the workweek by the number of hours worked [5 CFR 551.501(a)(4)].
gold_answer: 1.5 times the regular rate for hours over 8 in a day or 40 in a workweek [5 CFR 551.501(a)]

question: How many hours is the basic workweek for a full-time federal employee?
answer: The basic workweek for a full-time federal employee is 40 hours, as specified in [5 CFR 610.111(a)(1)]. This workweek does not extend over more than 6 of any 7 consecutive days.
gold_answer: 40 hours, not over more than 6 of any 7 consecutive days [5 CFR 610.111(a)(1)]

question: How long do I need to have worked for the government before I can use FMLA leave?
answer: To be eligible for FMLA leave, you must have at least 12 months of qualifying civilian or military service. This service does not need to be consecutive or recent and may include service at one or more agencies. Qualifying civilian service includes employment as defined in 5 U.S.C. 2105, such as with the United States Postal Service or a non-appropriated fund instrumentality. [OPM fact sheet: Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) 12-Week Entitlement > 12 Months of Qualifying Civilian or Military Service]
gold_answer: At least 12 months of service [5 U.S.C. 6381(1)(B)]

question: Can I take compensatory time off instead of being paid for irregular overtime?
answer: Yes, you may take compensatory time off instead of being paid for irregular or occasional overtime work, provided it is approved by your agency head or designee [5 CFR 550.114(a)]. This applies to both FLSA exempt and nonexempt employees who are covered by the definition of "employee" at 5 U.S.C. 5541(2) [OPM fact sheet: Compensatory Time Off > Employee Coverage]. However, no mandatory compensatory time off is permitted for wage employees in lieu of FLSA overtime pay [OPM fact sheet: Compensatory Time Off > Mandatory].
gold_answer: Yes, at the employee's request the agency may grant compensatory time off instead of overtime pay [5 CFR 550.114(a)]

question: What is the maximum recruitment incentive as a share of annual basic pay?
answer: The maximum recruitment incentive as a share of annual basic pay is 25 percent of the annual rate of basic pay of the employee at the beginning of the service period multiplied by the number of years (including fractions of a year) in the service period, unless a waiver is granted. [5 CFR 575.109(b)(1)]
gold_answer: Generally up to 25% of annual basic pay for the service period [5 CFR 575.109(b)(1)]

question: What is the maximum retention incentive an individual employee can be authorized?
answer: The maximum retention incentive an individual employee can be authorized is 50 percent of the employee's basic pay, as provided under § 575.309(e)(1). This authorization requires a waiver of the usual limit, which is typically 25 percent, and is contingent upon a critical agency need and the employee's unique qualifications. [5 CFR 575.309(a)(1), (e)(1)]
gold_answer: 25% of basic pay for an individual employee [5 CFR 575.309(a)(1)]

question: I'm at GS step 2. How long must I wait for my next within-grade increase?
answer: For an employee at GS step 2, the required waiting period for the next within-grade increase to step 3 is 52 weeks of creditable service in step 2 [OPM fact sheet: Within-Grade Increases > Required Waiting Periods]. This applies to employees with a scheduled tour of duty. The waiting period begins on the first appointment as an employee of the Federal Government or on receiving an equivalent increase [5 CFR 531.405(b)].
gold_answer: 52 calendar weeks of creditable service (steps 1–3) [5 CFR 531.405(a)]

question: How long is the waiting period between step 5 and step 6?
answer: The waiting period between step 5 and step 6 is 104 weeks of creditable service in step 5 [OPM fact sheet: Within-Grade Increases > Required Waiting Periods].
gold_answer: 104 calendar weeks (steps 4–6) [5 CFR 531.405(a)]

question: How long is the wait for a within-grade increase once I'm at step 7 or above?
answer: The waiting period for a within-grade increase once you are at step 7 or above is 156 calendar weeks of creditable service in that step [OPM fact sheet: Within-Grade Increases > Required Waiting Periods]. This applies to employees with a scheduled tour of duty [5 CFR 531.405].
gold_answer: 156 calendar weeks [5 CFR 531.405(a)(iii)]

question: What is the most administrative leave an agency can place an employee on in a calendar year?
answer: The most administrative leave an agency can place an employee on in a calendar year is 10 workdays, as specified in 5 U.S.C. 6329a(b)(1) and 5 CFR 630.1404(a). This limit applies specifically to administrative leave for investigative purposes. For other purposes, there is no specified annual limit. [5 U.S.C. 6329a(b)(1)] [5 CFR 630.1404(a)]
gold_answer: No more than 10 work days per calendar year [5 U.S.C. 6329a(b)(1)]

question: When does the federal leave year begin?
answer: The federal leave year begins on the first day of the first full biweekly pay period in a calendar year [OPM fact sheet: Leave Year Beginning and Ending Dates > Fact Sheet: Leave Year Beginning and Ending Dates].
gold_answer: On the first day of the first full biweekly pay period in the calendar year [OPM fact sheet: Leave Year]

question: If my office closes for a snowstorm, can my agency give me paid leave?
answer: Yes, if your office closes due to a snowstorm, your agency may grant you paid leave under the weather and safety leave provisions. [5 U.S.C. 6329c(b)(1)] This leave is provided without loss of pay and is available when you are prevented from safely traveling to or performing work at an approved location due to an act of God, such as a weather emergency. Agencies must also record this leave separately from other types of leave. [5 U.S.C. 6329c(c)]
gold_answer: Yes, weather and safety leave without loss of pay may be approved [5 U.S.C. 6329c(b)]

question: Do I have to agree to keep working for my agency after taking paid parental leave?
answer: Yes, you must agree in writing to work for your agency for not less than 12 weeks beginning on your first scheduled workday after paid parental leave concludes [5 CFR 630.1705(a)]. This agreement can be a handwritten signature, an electronic signature, or a documented email/text message with a signature within 24 hours [5 CFR 630.1705(b)(1)]. Failure to return for the required 12 weeks may result in reimbursement requirements for health insurance contributions [5 CFR 630.1705(f)].
gold_answer: Yes, you must agree in writing beforehand to work for the agency for at least 12 weeks after the leave ends [5 U.S.C. 6382(d)(2)]

question: Is there a minimum length of service to be eligible for paid parental leave?
answer: Yes, there is a minimum length of service requirement. Employees must complete at least 12 months of service as an employee within the meaning of section 6381(1)(A) before the date of the applicable birth or placement to be eligible for paid parental leave [5 U.S.C. 6382(d)(2)(iii)(E)]. Additionally, employees with temporary appointments, intermittent work schedules, or fewer than 12 months of qualifying Federal service are not eligible for PPL [OPM fact sheet: Paid Parental Leave > Key Features of PPL].
gold_answer: Yes, at least 12 months of service before the birth or placement [5 U.S.C. 6382(d)(2)]
